scope: Opt-in hardware acceptance of the flow-controlled Incus relay on an isolated appliance (task 3.4). Relay evidence only; not ZFS qualification.

macus.build: release, ad-hoc signed with the virtualization entitlement

deviation: The guest payload carried an uncommitted pin bump to linux-lts/zfs-lts 6.18.62-r0 because Alpine v3.24 no longer serves the committed 6.18.60-r0 pair. That payload revision (ea1aa733ed6010bcea293df9ad51e2b48f1f6c69b3dbae027c55e2a7cc23deaa) was used only for this run; the kernel/ZFS pair is unqualified and this run is not ZFS evidence.

relay_pipe.description: One incus.sock connection streams a 1.04 GiB uncompressed image export while a second connection uploads the same bytes as an image import into another project, so guest-to-host and host-to-guest data cross the vsock device at once (the relay-migration pattern). New-connection /1.0 probes ran every 250 ms throughout.

not_counted: An `incus copy --mode relay` between two remote names for the same socket completed server-side because the client detects the same server, so it is not recorded as relay evidence.
